 Presented by Updates: Lawrence to IR, Liufau returns
 Nov 06, 2026 at 02:00 PM DallasCowboys.com Dallas Cowboys Staff Writers
 Copied! 
 Nov. 7
 Malachi Lawrence
 #57 OLB 
 Height: 6-4 
 Weight: 253 lbs 
 College: UCF 
 1:43 p.m. --  The Cowboys officially placed OLB Malachi Lawrence on injured reserve ahead of their Week 9 matchup against the Colts.
 Earlier in the week, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Lawrence could potentially miss several weeks with an ankle injury. Now, he'll miss at least the next four games. Lawrence will be eligible to return as early as Dallas' Week 13 matchup against the Seahawks.
 The good news for Dallas is they get help back at outside linebacker, as the team activated Marist Liufau off IR/DTR. Should he be active on Sunday, it'll mark Liufau's regular season debut.
 Jordan Hudson
 #81 WR 
 Height: 6-1 
 Weight: 199 lbs 
 College: SMU 
 1:42 p.m. --  Ahead of their Week 9 matchup against Indianapolis, the Cowboys elevated WR Jordan Hudson and TE James Mitchell from the practice squad to the active roster.
 Mitchell makes his second straight appearance for Dallas as TEs Jake Ferguson (ankle) and Luke Schoonmaker (groin) are questionable for Sunday. Mitchell fell on a fumble in the end zone against Arizona for a touchdown last week.
 Hudson, rookie WR from SMU, is elevated for the first time this season. The Cowboys will once again be without WR KaVontae Turpin (ribs), and WR George Pickens is questionable with a hamstring injury.
 Nov. 6
 Caleb Downs
 #13 DB 
 Height: 6-0 
 Weight: 210 lbs 
 College: Ohio State 
 2:02 p.m. -- Unfortunately, the Cowboys are again fighting against the injury after nearly being whole only a couple of weeks ago.
 On their latest injury report, versus the Colts, they've officially ruled out both KaVontae Turpin (ribs) for yet another week and, for the first time this season, Malachi Lawrence (ankle) has been ruled out -- an IR candidate.
 The good news, however, is that Caleb Downs and PJ Locke have both cleared concussion protocol and will play in Indy.
 Those listed as questionable include Joey Porter Jr. (ankle), Jake Ferguson (ankle), DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back), George Pickens (shoulder/ankle), Luke Schoonmaker (groin) -- Jonathan Bullard (calf) and Marist Liufau (wrist) as well, though they are on IR unless activated this week.
 -------------------
 Nov. 5
 Joey Porter Jr.
 #25 CB 
 Height: 6-2 
 Weight: 194 lbs 
 College: Penn State 
 4:00 p.m. --  Cowboys CB Joey Porter Jr., who was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, bumped down to limited participation on Thursday.
 In good news for Dallas, DB Caleb Downs (concussion/ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion) were upgraded to limited participation Thursday. Both are still in the NFL's concussion protocol.
 LB DeMarvion Overshown popped up on the injury repot as a limited participant with a hamstring/back injury. Fellow LB Dee Winters was a full participant after being limited with a calf injury.
 For the full injury report, click here. 
 Nov. 4
 George Pickens
 #3 WR 
 Height: 6-3 
 Weight: 205 lbs 
 College: Georgia 
 3:47 p.m. --  Cowboys WR George Pickens (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice as the Cowboys prepare for the Colts on Sunday.
 TE Luke Schoonmaker (groin), G Tyler Smith (ankle) and LB Dee Winters (calf) were also limited on Wednesday. CB Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) was a full participant after dealing with the ankle injury late against the Cardinals.
 DB Caleb Downs (concussion/ankle) and S P.J. Locke (concussion) did not practice as they continue to work through concussion protocol.
 For the full injury report, click here. 
 Jalen Thompson
 #34 S 
 Height: 5-11 
 Weight: 190 lbs 
 College: Washington State 
 12:30 p.m. - Just as the Cowboys were getting whole on defense from injury, they're forced to place Caleb Downs and PJ Locke in the league's concussion protocol following the Week 8 matchup against the Cardinals.
 That strikes another blow to the safeties room because though Downs has mostly played slot corner, he has also been deployed to aid the ailing safety depth chart — one that is still without Jalen Thompson.
 Thompson suffered a hamstring early in the season and has been rehabilitating the injury since. He qualified to have his 21-day practice window activated this week but, on Wednesday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer stated Thompson's window has not yet been opened.
 The Cowboys do have the remainder of the week to change their mind, but Thompson was also without pads during the open portion of practice, a sign he may still not be ready for Week 9.
 Nov. 3
 Ryan Flournoy
 #19 WR 
 Height: 6-1 
 Weight: 205 lbs 
 College: Southeast Missouri State 
 2:43 p.m. - With 32 teams in the NFL, one might assume every team in the league has that true WR1 that is the go-to receiver. And while every team is built differently, some with more of a run-first mentality and others that incorporate the tight end more in the offense, there are some interesting stats for Ryan Flournoy this year.
 After eight games, Flournoy ranks third on the team with 342 yards, which is no real surprise, considering he was always expected to be behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
 However, Lamb ranks third in the NFL with 709 yards and Pickens is 14th with 533. But Flournoy is 31st among all wide receivers with 342 yards. Shockingly enough, he's got more yards than Minnesota's Justin Jefferson, who has just 335 yards in six games.
 In fact, Jefferson and the Vikings are among the seven teams in the NFL whose No. 1 wide receiver has less yards than Flournoy, who also has two touchdown catches this year. Flournoy needs 133 yards to surpass last year's career-high total of 475 yards for a season.
 -------------------
 Nov. 2
 Jake Ferguson
 #87 TE 
 Height: 6-5 
 Weight: 250 lbs 
 College: Wisconsin 
 5:18 p.m. - The Cowboys got some encouraging news on Monday about tight end Jake Ferguson, who missed most of the game Sunday with an ankle injury.
 Despite suffering the first-quarter injury and not returning to action, Ferguson actually has a chance to practice this week and potentially play against the Colts.
 Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that the tests came back clean on Ferguson and the team will monitor his status this week but there's hope he could play. The Cowboys were already without Luke Schoonmaker as well on Sunday, leaving only Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell to play at tight end. Mitchell recovered a fumble in the end zone for a touchdown.
 -----------------
 P.J. Locke
 #1 S 
 Height: 5-10 
 Weight: 205 lbs 
 College: Texas 
 5:12 p.m. - Just after he returned to action for the first time in over a month, safety P.J. Locke was injured again on Sunday.
 Locke suffered a head injury and remains in the concussion protocol on Monday, according to Brian Schottenheimer.
 Locke had a foot injury that put him on IR-to return since this week. He was moved back to the roster but now his status for Sunday's game in Indianapolis remains in question.
 --------------
 Caleb Downs
 #13 DB 
 Height: 6-0 
 Weight: 210 lbs 
 College: Ohio State 
 2:20 p.m. --  Cowboys rookie DB Caleb Downs is in concussion protocol, according to Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer.
 Downs will now have to go through the five-step return to participation process in order to return to action, and will have a full week to attempt to be cleared before Dallas' Week 9 game against the Colts in Indianapolis.
 In 53 defensive snaps against Arizona, Downs recorded four tackles, none bigger than his run stuff of Jeremiyah Love on the goal line as the Cardinals faced fourth and goal.
 Nov. 1
 Luke Schoonmaker
 #86 TE 
 Height: 6-5 
 Weight: 250 lbs 
 College: Michigan 
 Oct. 31
 10:30 a.m. -- As the Cowboys welcome back PJ Locke from injured reserve to try and land a much-needed victory over the Cardinals, they'll have to do without other key players.
 KaVontae Turpin and Dee Winters are still battling injury and, as such, headline the Week 8 inactives at AT&T Stadium — along with tight end Luke Schoonmaker, who missed practice(s) this week with a groin injury.
 Other inactives include Shavon Revel Jr., Tyrust Wheat and Drew Shelton.
 With Schoommaker missing the contest, the Cowboys elevated tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad.
 P.J. Locke
 #1 S 
 Height: 5-10 
 Weight: 205 lbs 
 College: Texas 
 1:14 p.m. --  The Cowboys have activated S P.J. Locke off Reserve/Injured-Designated for Return, giving the Cowboys added health in the safety room.
 In the past few weeks, the Cowboys have seen Caleb Downs, Markquese Bell and Alijah Clark all rotate at the safety position opposite Malik Hooker. Now, Locke could give them a more steadfast option.
 Additionally, the Cowboys elevated TE James Mitchell from the practice squad to the active roster. Fellow TE Luke Schoonmaker is questionable with a groin injury, and did not practice on Thursday and Friday. If Schoonmaker isn't available, Mitchell could be active Sunday afternoon for Dallas.
 Oct. 30
 George Pickens
 #3 WR 
 Height: 6-3 
 Weight: 205 lbs 
 College: Georgia 
 4:05 p.m. --  Cowboys WR George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) and DT Kenny Clark (back) are questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
 Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said earlier on Friday that Pickens is expected to play. Clark popped up Friday on the intjury report with the back injury, and was limited in practice.
 WR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and LB Dee Winters (calf) are officially out. Dallas' three players in their 21-day practice windows, DT Jonathan Bullard (calf), OLB Marist Liufau (forearm) and S P.J. Locke (foot) are all questionable. The Cowboys have an open spot on their 53-man roster, meaning if all three are activated, two corresponding moves would have to be made.
 For the full injury report, click here. 
 Oct. 29
 Caleb Downs
 #13 DB 
 Height: 6-0 
 Weight: 210 lbs 
 College: Ohio State 
 4:00 p.m. --  For the second day in a row, Cowboys DB Caleb Downs was limited in practice with an ankle injury.
 Additionally, DT Quinnen Williams (hamstring) and WR George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) were also limited for a second straight day.
 In his first practice back from the team opening his 21-day window, DT Jonathan Bullard (calf) was a full participant. TE Luke Schoonmaker popped up with a groin injury, and did not participate. G Tyler Smith also popped up with an ankle injury, but was a full participant.
 For the full injury report, click here. 
 Oct. 28
 George Pickens
 #3 WR 
 Height: 6-3 
 Weight: 205 lbs 
 College: Georgia 
 5 p.m. - The Cowboys came out of Philadelphia with both a win and mostly intact, a rarity for Dallas this season.
 That said, there are a few who are "nursing bumps and bruises" as described by head coach Brian Schottenheimer, and that includes Caleb Downs (ankle) being limited on Wednesday.
 George Pickens continues to work through a shoulder injury and, now, a hamstring issue as well that caused him to be limited in practice; and Quinnen Williams is also nursing a minor hamstring issue. Neither KaVontae Turpin (ribs) nor Dee Winters (calf) participated in practice.
 Drew Shelton (hamstring) returned in a limited capacity, and the added good news is that both Marist Liufau (arm) and PJ Locke (foot) both continue to fully participate as they work toward returning to the field.
 Oct. 27
 Brian Schottenheimer
 Head Coach
 College: Florida 
 Hometown: Denver, CO 
 5:21 p.m. - Aside from all of the years he's been coaching in the NFL, Brian Schottenheimer learned about criticism at an early age, getting a front-row seat to the coaching life with his dad, Marty Schottenheimer serving as an NFL head coach for over 20 years.
 So when the Cowboys struggled on offense and his play-calling duties were even questioned, Schotty responded with his best effort of the season on Monday. Was it because of the criticism? Schotty said on Monday in his press conference he does his best to focus on the task at hand for himself and the players.
 "We're motivated as a football team, I'm motivated as a head coach to get our guys playing to the standard that I know they're capable of playing. Intense game against a real rival," Schotty said. "I'll be honest I really do a good job of blocking you guys out.
 "Remember you're talking to a guy that grew up for 25 years in a household with a head coach in the NFL. So, no, it was more just my focus was getting the team to be focused and motivated. And I think you saw that (Monday) night, so I'm proud of our group."
